comparison: Perfect agreement on clinical phenotype (C1, C18, C19). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the foundational patient observation of elevated BMD with hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on dimerization findings (C2, C20-C25). Both evaluations support the western blot evidence for dimeric formation and the proteasome inhibition experiments. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the dimerization as a key strength.

Strong agreement on altered signaling properties (C26-C29, C69, C104). Both evaluations support the binding and cAMP signaling data showing reduced potency but maintained maximal response. Peer reviewers explicitly note receptor activation as compelling.

Perfect agreement on acute in vivo responses (C4, C30-C33, C70). Both evaluations support the calcemic and phosphaturic effects demonstrated in time-course experiments. Peer reviewers affirm the translational aspects as fundamental.

Perfect agreement on bone formation in intact mice (C5, C34, C71). Both evaluations support the calvarial injection model showing 4-fold increase in new bone width. Peer reviewers confirm the anabolic potential as a study strength.

Strong agreement on bone anabolic effects in OVX model (C6, C35-C47, C64). Both evaluations support the comprehensive μ-CT analysis showing differential effects on cortical vs. trabecular bone. OpenEval notes concerns about bone strength despite improved parameters, but peer reviewers accept the overall characterization as compelling.

Overlapping coverage of biomechanical testing (C48-C51). OpenEval notes the lack of bone strength improvement raises questions about bone quality, while peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge as part of the overall characterization.

Strong agreement on differential bone marker effects (C52-C55, C79-C80). Both evaluations support the finding that dimeric R25CPTH stimulates bone formation without suppressing resorption, distinguishing it from wild-type PTH. Peer reviewers accept this as a key differentiating finding.

Agreement on osteoclast activity findings (C56-C59). OpenEval supports the histological data on osteoclast parameters, while peer reviewers accept these findings as supporting the distinct mechanism of action without raising concerns.

Agreement on safety profile (C65-C66). Both evaluations support the lack of hypercalcemia and excessive resorption as key translational advantages. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the anabolic mechanism and safety as compelling.

Perfect agreement on vertebral bone findings (C60-C63). Both evaluations support the trabecular improvements in vertebrae with similar effects between treatments. Peer reviewers accept the findings without challenge.
Perfect agreement on citation of prior work (C67-C68). Both evaluations accept the references to Lee et al., 2015 as appropriate context. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Agreement on speculative mechanistic claims (C73-C78). Both evaluations rate these as uncertain/speculative. OpenEval notes lack of direct structural data, while peer reviewers do not explicitly address but appear to accept as appropriate speculation given no revision requests.

Agreement on interpretive claims (C81-C83). Both evaluations rate these as uncertain/speculative. OpenEval notes causal connections are not established, while peer reviewers do not explicitly comment but accept the work as complete without requesting additional mechanistic investigation.

OpenEval evaluated extensive background/context claims (C7-C17, C85-C103) as appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.
OpenEval evaluated citation to Andersen et al., 2022 (C84) as supported and important for understanding human phenotype. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate this specific citation.

Overlapping coverage of cAMP signaling conclusion (C104). OpenEval provides separate evaluation of this summary claim as supported by Figure 2B data. Peer reviewers include this within their broader evaluation of signaling properties (R3) without separate assessment.
